lead_headline: Restaurant tracker logs 3 new leads today—High Point Creamery joins McGregor Square food hall, Ariel's Cafe opens in Montbello FreshLo Hub—while foreclosure filings jump 37% week-over-week to 48

restaurant.blurb: 3 new leads today (2 openings, 1 closure) bring active inventory to 91 (47 openings, 44 closures)—Monday additions include High Point Creamery debuting at McGregor Square Food & Drink's Union Station food hall (confidence 8), Ariel's Cafe launching Black woman-owned coffee shop in Montbello's FreshLo Hub after February soft open (confidence 9). Closure: Los Dos Amigos Tacos and Tortas food truck vanished from Englewood's South Broadway (confidence 8). Today's 3-lead haul trails weekend's 9-case surge but extends April's opening bias—week's 91 active cases split 52% openings versus 48% closures, reversing March's closure-heavy 56/44 tilt. McGregor Square placement marks fourth Union Station corridor opening in 10 days (C Burger, Ogo Korean BBQ, Mendocino Farms, High Point) as downtown food hall density accelerates.

foreclosure.blurb: 48 filings this week surge 37% from last week's 35-case baseline, with Douglas County's $1.1M Beebalm Loop estate topping the roster as zero $2M+ properties enter the pipeline—92 auctions queue for next seven days while $15.2M total filing value trails last week's $18M+ haul.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today push statewide filing freeze to 38 consecutive days—Monday marks eighth straight zero-filing session as April's opening week posts 0/8 shutout, now 217% beyond December 2024's 12-day record drought. No Liquor Enforcement Division bulletins, no legislative freeze signals, no industry association alerts—system paralysis enters sixth week with backlog estimate climbing to 80-110 applications. Database shows 13,732 historical entries but zero March 1–April 7 activity across all Colorado counties, all license types (retail, tavern, hotel/restaurant, brew pub, distillery), all application categories (new, renewal, transfer, modification). Void obliterates all seasonal precedent including January-February's typical 15-20 weekly baseline.

reputation.blurb: 7 mentions yesterday lift week's tally to 53 citations (−12% vs prior week's 60) across 15 sources—this week's leaders: Denver Post (13 mentions), Instagram (11), Facebook (10), with traditional/social split holding 70/30. Notable Monday pickups include Denver Post's bank fraud lawsuit coverage, Instagram Cherry Creek luxury living feature, Facebook business boom commentary. Source count dips one outlet from last week's 16 while daily mention rate slides to 7.6/day from 8.6/day prior period, snapping March's upward trajectory and returning to February baseline despite maintained source diversity.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (2 new, 3 canceled) drags MTD to −1 (−0.14/day through 7 days) while 90-day net holds +137. Monday's churn mirrors Sunday's pattern—past week delivers +6 net (16 new, 10 canceled) versus prior week's +22 (35 new, 13 canceled), marking 73% net slowdown despite comparable cancellation rates (10 vs 13). Seven-day April start posts −1 net (15 new, 16 canceled, −0.14/day) versus March's opening week (+29 net, +4.1/day), confirming 103% reversal. Last 14 days split cleanly: March 24-31 roared +22 net (30 new, 8 canceled, +2.8/day), April 1-7 stumbled −16 net (15 new, 31 canceled, −2.3/day)—acquisition cratered 50% while cancellations quadrupled, flipping +2.8/day March momentum to −2.3/day April drag. YTD +130 (+1.4/day) cushions monthly hemorrhage but current pace projects −4 April finish, requiring immediate 34-subscriber turnaround to restore Q1 trajectory.
